chunks: Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! What is the reward for one who visits the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) with intention?' He replied, 'Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.a.w.) with intention?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) underscores the immense spiritual merit of visiting the Prophet’s shrine with deliberate devotion, linking physical pilgrimage directly to eternal salvation. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s enduring presence and the tangible rewards of honoring his legacy through *Ziyarah*. This tradition serves as a foundational text for the practice of visiting the Prophet’s tomb in Medina as an act of worship.
